reuse.why: The range handler reuses the same schedule construction and getDateWithSkippedWeekend as getUpcomingDates/getNextDate, and a new createRecurSchedule factory replaces the duplicated RSchedule construction in rule-utils and app.ts.

duplication.why: The daily-skip rule is encoded once in the recurrence (byDayOfWeek + holiday exrules) so no call site re-decides it; the only repetition is MM-DD/full-date holiday matching expressed both as exrules and in getDateWithSkippedWeekend's isHoliday.

placement.why: Recurrence building and weekend/holiday resolution live in shared/schedules.ts; the server handler only filters the window and registers the method.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps, with tests and a release note; no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: One factory and one resolver own the rule, so callers stay simple; the window margin heuristic (2 + 3 per holiday) and the dual holiday representation are slightly subtle.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend-aware schedule construction goes through createRecurSchedule; find-schedules.ts still builds RSchedule directly but has no weekend handling.

disguised_duplication.where: Holiday matching (full date vs MM-DD) is implemented twice in different shapes: as RSchedule exrules in getHolidayExrules and as the isHoliday closure in getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily+skipWeekend weekday branch; all callers use the shared factory/resolver.
